explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. God says, 'Because you exclaimed, "Aha!" when My sanctuary was profaned, when the land of Israel was laid waste, and when the house of Judah went into exile' (Ezekiel 25:3). One little word, and it's what God brings up. I think that's a word you want back the second it leaves your mouth.

Nope, nobody's setting up roadblocks in this passage. The text says the Ammonites exclaimed, "Aha!" (Ezekiel 25:3). No orange cones, no detour signs. God points to how they reacted when the sanctuary was profaned, the land was laid waste and Judah went into exile.

That's a good guess, but it isn't what the text says. The Ammonites aren't charged with grabbing anything here. They exclaimed, "Aha!" when the sanctuary was profaned, the land was laid waste and Judah went into exile (Ezekiel 25:3). It was their reaction God points to, and the reaction was one word.

Camels it is! God says, 'I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels, and Ammon a resting place for sheep' (Ezekiel 25:5). Rabbah was a city, and God says it'll be a camel pasture. Then the verse ends with 'Then you will know that I am the LORD.'

Close, since it's a four-legged animal, but not the one. God says, 'I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels' (Ezekiel 25:5). Horses don't make the list in this verse. Only camels and sheep do, and sheep were already assigned to Ammon.

I see why you'd go there, friend, because goats love a pasture. But the verse says, 'I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels, and Ammon a resting place for sheep' (Ezekiel 25:5). Camels for Rabbah, sheep for Ammon. No goats get a mention.

True! Right after the camels and the sheep, God says, 'Then you will know that I am the LORD' (Ezekiel 25:5). That line shows up again and again in this chapter. Whatever happens, God says they'll know exactly who He is.

It's actually true. God ends the verse with, 'Then you will know that I am the LORD' (Ezekiel 25:5). It's a line you'll hear again and again in this chapter. The Ammonites aren't left guessing about who is speaking.

Contempt is right. God says they 'clapped your hands and stomped your feet and rejoiced over the land of Israel with a heart full of contempt' (Ezekiel 25:6). Contempt means looking down on somebody. Rejoicing over a neighbor's trouble while looking down on them is a heavy way to cheer.

Envy sounds like it could fit, but it isn't the word God uses. He says the Ammonites rejoiced 'with a heart full of contempt' (Ezekiel 25:6). Envy wants what the other person has. Contempt looks down on them, and that's the word in the verse.

Greed is a fair guess, friend, but not what the verse says. The Ammonites rejoiced over the land of Israel 'with a heart full of contempt' (Ezekiel 25:6). The verse names what was in their hearts, and it's contempt, not greed.

Careful, this one flips the verse. God says the opposite: 'I will cut you off from the peoples and exterminate you from the countries' (Ezekiel 25:7). So the Ammonites don't keep their place among the peoples. That's a heavy line, and it's good to read it slowly.

False is right. God says, 'I will cut you off from the peoples and exterminate you from the countries. I will destroy you, and you will know that I am the LORD' (Ezekiel 25:7). Keeping their place is the opposite of what He says. I think this one is heavy, so it's worth reading slowly.

explanations.answer: Judah is like all the other nations
explanations.explanation: That's it. Moab and Seir said, 'Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations' (Ezekiel 25:8). That's what God brings up. Then He says, 'therefore I will indeed expose the flank of Moab' (Ezekiel 25:9). Said out loud, and God heard it.

explanations.answer: Judah will soon rise up again
explanations.explanation: That would've been a kinder thing to say, friend, but it's not what the verse has. Moab and Seir said, 'Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations' (Ezekiel 25:8). Nothing in it says Judah will rise again. The words they said put Judah in the same bunch as every other nation.

explanations.answer: Judah is greater than every nation
explanations.explanation: If only, because that'd be a compliment! But the verse shows the opposite attitude. Moab and Seir said, 'Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations' (Ezekiel 25:8). They saw Judah as ordinary, not as greater than everybody.

explanations.answer: They will no longer be remembered
explanations.explanation: Right. God says He'll give Moab and the Ammonites to the people of the East, 'so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations' (Ezekiel 25:10). It's a sobering line. A people that cheered over Judah's trouble ends up forgotten.

explanations.answer: They will be honored once again
explanations.explanation: That's not what God says, friend. The verse says the Ammonites will be given as a possession to the people of the East, 'so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations' (Ezekiel 25:10). Honor isn't in the picture. Being forgotten is.

explanations.answer: They will rule over the nations
explanations.explanation: Nope, the verse goes the other direction. God says the Ammonites will be given as a possession to the people of the East, 'so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations' (Ezekiel 25:10). Ruling over the nations isn't in the picture. I think this one is a heavy line.

True. God says, 'Because Edom acted vengefully against the house of Judah, and in so doing incurred grievous guilt' (Ezekiel 25:12). Grievous is a serious word. God doesn't treat this as a small thing, and the verse says it plainly.

It's actually true. The verse says Edom 'acted vengefully against the house of Judah, and in so doing incurred grievous guilt' (Ezekiel 25:12). Grievous is a serious word. God doesn't treat this as a small thing.

You got it. God says, 'I will take My vengeance on Edom by the hand of My people Israel' (Ezekiel 25:14). Edom acted vengefully against the house of Judah, and God names His people Israel as the hand He'll use. It's His vengeance, carried out by the hand of Israel.

Good thinking, since the people of the East show up earlier in the chapter. God says He will give Ammon and Moab to them as a possession (Ezekiel 25:4, 10). But for Edom, God says, 'I will take My vengeance on Edom by the hand of My people Israel' (Ezekiel 25:14). Different nation, different hand.

The Egyptians don't show up anywhere in this chapter, friend. God says, 'I will take My vengeance on Edom by the hand of My people Israel' (Ezekiel 25:14). He names His own people as the hand He'll use.

Careful, because this one's a trap. God says Israel 'will deal with Edom according to My anger and wrath' (Ezekiel 25:14). That's His anger, not Israel's. The standard is God's own, and not what Israel happens to feel.

False is right. God says they 'will deal with Edom according to My anger and wrath' (Ezekiel 25:14). It's His anger and wrath that sets the standard. Israel's own feelings aren't what the verse points to.

Ancient is the word. God says the Philistines acted 'with malice of soul to destroy Judah with ancient hostility' (Ezekiel 25:15). That hostility is called ancient. It's a heavy verse, and the word says a lot.

Sudden sounds possible, but it's not the word in the verse. The Philistines acted 'with malice of soul to destroy Judah with ancient hostility' (Ezekiel 25:15). The verse calls the hostility ancient. It doesn't use the word sudden.
Secret is a fair guess, friend, but it's not the word. The verse says 'ancient hostility' (Ezekiel 25:15). Nothing in it calls the hostility hidden. It just says it had been around a long, long time.

Yes, the Cherethites! God says, 'I will stretch out My hand against the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the coast' (Ezekiel 25:16). He names them right alongside the Philistines. It's a serious word from the Lord GOD, and it's good to know who's named.

Not this time, friend. The Amalekites aren't named in this verse. God says, 'I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the coast' (Ezekiel 25:16). The Cherethites are the name the verse gives.

Good name, friend, but it's not in this verse. God says, 'I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the coast' (Ezekiel 25:16). The Cherethites are the ones named alongside the Philistines.

True. God says, 'I will execute great vengeance against them with furious reproof. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I lay My vengeance upon them' (Ezekiel 25:17). That's how the chapter closes. It's a heavy verse, and it's plainly there in the text.

It's actually true. The verse says, 'I will execute great vengeance against them with furious reproof' (Ezekiel 25:17). Then it adds that they will know He is the LORD. It's a heavy verse, and it's plainly there in the text.
